title: Pipeline validator settings file
description: The machine-readable definition of docs/PIPELINE-CONTRACT.md §23 — what the validator may approve, as plain on/off switches (scripts/pipeline_validator_settings.py, KIT-533): one switch each for plans, pieces and merges, the size limits, and one switch each for the four human-only classes the owner may allow. An absent file, or one that is not a valid, trusted settings file, means every switch is off.
$comment: NO SWITCH FOR THE SAFETY SYSTEM. Changes to hooks, guards, CI and workflows, branch protection and rulesets, settings, the watcher and the validator's own limits stay human, fixed in code; the loader refuses a file that names one. Nothing gains or loses trust by itself: only the owner edits this file, and the loader has no write path.

schema.description: The marker. A reader that does not know it treats every switch as off.

approve.description: What the validator may approve in the owner's place. Each is on (true) or off (false).

plans.description: A plan, in place of the owner's `approve <plan>`.

pieces.description: A ready piece of an approved plan starting.

merges.description: A pull request merging: a job asks GitHub to enable its own auto-merge. No agent merges.

limits.description: How big a change it may approve. 0 means nothing passes.

allow.description: The four human-only classes the owner may allow. Off (false) keeps a change in that class for the owner.

credentials.description: Env files, keys, tokens, secrets stores.

billing_and_accounts.description: Billing, accounts, the plan or subscription.

production_deploy.description: The deploy workflow and its config.

deleting_data.description: Migrations that drop, bulk deletes, branch or release removal.
